headline: First edition of the migration tab. Pressure from Belarus is concentrated on Latvia, where attempted illegal crossings in 2026 already exceed the whole of 2025, and Latvia wants to keep its special border regime until mid-2027. On the EU side, the Baltic states are formally classed as at risk and cannot be made to accept relocated migrants; no transfers of migrants to the Baltic states from other EU countries have been reported.
pressure_note: Latvia's border guard says 12,857 people were stopped trying to cross from Belarus by 10 November, above the 12,046 for all of 2025; recent daily figures are in the tens. Smugglers, tunnels and damage to border equipment continue. Lithuania and Poland see far fewer attempts, and Estonia closes its road crossings with Russia on 1 December.
eu_note: Under the EU Migration Pact each country chooses whether to take people, pay or send other support; Latvia and Lithuania say they will not take relocated migrants, and Estonia may ask to have its share reduced. The 2027 round is being negotiated after the Commission's 6 November report. Germany is resuming returns under EU rules to Italy and Greece, not the Baltic states.
changed: First edition, so there is no earlier day to compare with. Counts cover items reported between 10 and 17 November; from tomorrow they cover only what is new since the previous edition.
bottom_line: The evidence points to two different kinds of risk. The immediate one is pressure organised from Belarus: Latvian prosecutors describe smuggling networks, payments of about 5,000 dollars a crossing, migrants pushed to damage border equipment and suspected involvement of Belarusian border officials, which fits the hybrid pressure described in Lithuania's 2026 threat assessment. The second, which many people fear, is that other EU countries will shift their migrants onto the Baltic states. Under current rules that is limited: relocation is voluntary in practice, fewer than 1,000 people are expected to be physically relocated across the whole EU in 2026, and the Baltic states have declined to take any. The lawful channel that could grow is returns of people who first entered the EU through Latvia or Lithuania and moved on west; Poland already checks its border with Lithuania until March 2027 and turns people back. Claims that the EU forces the Baltic states to take thousands of migrants are not supported by the rules or the numbers. Daily crossing numbers swing widely and are published unevenly, so single days say little.

headline: Lithuania moves to take no relocated migrants under the EU solidarity scheme and pay instead, replacing a May pledge to take 58 from Cyprus; in Estonia, parties argue over checks on the Latvian border. No new organised crossing incidents or transfers of migrants to the Baltic states were reported.
pressure_note: No new daily crossing figures were found since the previous edition. The latest: Latvia stopped 12,857 attempts by 10 November; Lithuania turned back 1,896 people by 7 November, already more than the 1,652 in all of 2025; Poland recorded 482 attempts by 8 November and plans to extend its Belarus border buffer zone to 27 February 2027, citing drones and balloons. Belarus also ordered a snap readiness check of its border-guard units.
eu_note: A Lithuanian government commission approved the interior minister's proposal to take no relocated migrants and pay into the EU solidarity pool instead; the government still has to approve it and the amount is not yet known. The Pact allows this choice. Five EU states announced a Rwanda return hub for rejected asylum seekers, which Estonia supports but will not join; it does not change Baltic obligations. No transfers to the Baltic states were reported.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30, with no rating changes; trends move from New to Unchanged. All five counts are 0 (yesterday: organised incidents 1, new border measures 2, misleading claims 2). New since yesterday: Lithuania's plan to pay instead of relocating anyone; the Estonian party debate on checks at the Latvian border; the Rwanda return hub. Catching up: Poland's draft to extend its Belarus buffer zone (14 November) and Lithuania's year-to-date figure. Correction: yesterday's edition said the Baltic states have declined to take any relocated migrants; in fact Lithuania agreed in May to take 58 from Cyprus, a choice it is now moving to replace with a payment.
bottom_line: Today's news mostly concerns how the Baltic states use the choices the EU rules give them, not anything imposed on them. Lithuania's move to pay rather than relocate shows that the solidarity scheme lets a country refuse relocation entirely, which again contradicts claims that the EU forces the Baltic states to take migrants; it also shows that Lithuania had earlier volunteered to take a small group, so the picture is a national choice, not a refusal from the start. The organised pressure from Belarus continues on the evidence of recent weeks, with Latvia most affected and Lithuania's own turn-backs now above last year's total, although no fresh daily figures were published in this window. The Estonian debate on checks at the Latvian border is about onward movement inside Schengen and is partly driven by opposition parties; the government is not proposing checks. No other EU country has been reported planning to send migrants to the Baltic states; lawful returns between EU states remain a separate and, for now, quiet channel.

headline: Lithuania's interior minister rejects accusations of xenophobia over his plan to pay into the EU solidarity pool instead of taking relocated migrants, saying it is cheaper. Lithuania recorded no crossing attempts from Belarus for three days while Latvia stopped 88 in four days; Estonia puts the cost of checks on the Latvian border at €65 million and sees no need for them now.
pressure_note: New figures: Lithuania recorded no attempts to cross from Belarus outside official crossing points on 15–17 November after turning back seven people on 14 November, bringing its 2026 total to 1,962 against 1,652 in all of 2025. Latvia stopped 12, 41, 29 and 6 attempts on 14–17 November. The pressure remains concentrated on Latvia. Figures count attempts, not people, and are published unevenly.
eu_note: No EU decision, transfer or plan to send migrants to the Baltic states was reported. Lithuania's interior minister repeated that the country will pay into the solidarity pool next year rather than accept relocated people, and said the decision is political and financial; the amount is not yet set. This is a choice the Pact allows. Poland and Estonia are exempt from contributing.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30, with no rating changes, and all five counts stay at 0. New since yesterday: fresh border figures from Lithuania (three days with no attempts, 1,962 so far this year) and Latvia (88 attempts on 14–17 November); Lithuania's interior minister rejected xenophobia accusations and said paying is cheaper than relocation over five years; Estonia's interior ministry put the cost of Latvian border checks at about €65 million and said they are not needed now; Estonia's parliament advanced the bill to close crossings with Russia. Catching up: an Estonian court report (16 November) on a plea-bargain conviction for driving five migrants from Latvia into Estonia.
bottom_line: Organised pressure from Belarus continues but is uneven: Latvia still stops dozens of attempts most days, while Lithuania has had a quiet spell, and day-to-day swings in these figures should not be read as a trend because they count attempts and are published irregularly. The EU side is quiet: no other EU state has been reported planning to send migrants to the Baltic states, and Lithuania's decision to pay rather than relocate again shows the solidarity scheme does not force anyone to take people. The minister's cost argument is plausible but unproven, since no figures have been published and the payment amount is not set. In Estonia, the government's own estimate and its statement that checks on the Latvian border are not needed now undercut opposition claims that onward migration through Latvia requires them, though the €65 million figure differs from earlier numbers in the debate. Lawful returns between EU states and pressure organised from Belarus remain separate issues, and only the second is active this week.

headline: Latvia's tally of prevented crossings from Belarus has passed 13,000 this year, above all of 2025 and nearing the 2023 record. Lithuania drafts a fence plan for parts of its Kaliningrad border. No EU decision or transfer that would send migrants to the Baltic states was reported.
pressure_note: No new daily border figures were published after 17 November in the sources found. Latvia's running total reached about 13,012 prevented attempts by 16 November (plus 6 on 17 November), against 12,046 in all of 2025 and a record 13,863 in 2023; border guards note the figures can count the same person several times. Lithuania recorded no attempts on 15–17 November and 1,962 so far this year. Pressure remains concentrated on Latvia.
eu_note: No new EU decision, transfer or plan to send migrants to the Baltic states. Under the Commission's 6 November assessment, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia are 'at risk' (priority access to EU support), and Estonia is also among six states facing a significant situation that may ask for reductions in their solidarity contributions. The Council is expected to set the 2027 solidarity pool before the end of the year.
changed: The migration pressure score is unchanged at 12 of 30, with no rating changes, and all five counts stay at 0. New since yesterday: Lithuania's border guard service presented a plan to fence parts of the Kaliningrad border, which still needs funding; a correction to our earlier wording, that Poland and Estonia are 'exempt' from the solidarity pool: the Commission lists them among states that may request deductions, which is not yet an exemption for 2027; Lithuania cut its 2027 quota for foreign workers to 24,400, a labour-migration matter separate from asylum. Catching up: Latvia's 2026 total passed 13,000 on 16 November, and Estonian police say over 400 people caught in Estonia this year were returned to Latvia under a bilateral arrangement.
bottom_line: Organised pressure from Belarus continues, and Latvia's year total now exceeds all of 2025, which supports the Elevated rating; but the totals count attempts, the same person may be counted several times, and no new daily figures appeared in the last two days, so no short-term trend can be drawn. On the EU side nothing new points to other states shifting migrants onto the Baltic states: the Commission's designations give all three priority access to support, and the main open question is the 2027 pool the Council still has to set. The only regular transfers involving the Baltic states found this week are lawful returns from Estonia to Latvia of people who moved north after crossing from Belarus, which is a consequence of the Belarus route, not a burden shifted from western Europe. Lithuania's Kaliningrad fence plan is aimed mainly at hybrid threats and possible Russian draft evaders, not at a current migration flow. Coverage that treats Lithuania's or Estonia's pool status as settled runs ahead of the decision, which has not been taken.
